incident.location: 160 block Dutchess Way, Rancho Cordova, CA
incident.summary: A woman called 911 to report an armed man (Christopher Paul Walker, 29) at her home. When deputies arrived, Walker shot the 58-year-old caller four times on the porch, killing her, then opened fire on deputies instead of fleeing — wounding Deputy Eric Schmidt in the leg. Walker died of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. Two dead; deputy recovered.

moments.summary: The 58-year-old victim calls 911 reporting the armed man at her home — the human voice of the person who will be killed minutes later. The emotional spine and likely cold-open.
Deputies arrive and approach on Dutchess Way; calm-before tension as they move toward the home. Establishes geography across the three bodycam POVs.

Walker, seeing deputies, shoots the 911 caller four times on the porch and kills her. The pivotal, horrifying turn — the victim is killed by the very person she called for protection from. Likely captured across multiple POVs (cross-cam sync target).
With escape routes available, Walker instead crouches near an A/C unit and opens fire on deputies — the decision that defines the gun battle.
Deputy Eric Schmidt is shot in the lower body during the exchange — the moment from the wounded deputy's own bodycam POV. Peak chaos.
Deputies return fire on Walker. The use-of-force core the AB748/SB16 release exists to document.
Walker dies of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head — the grim resolution that reframes the whole encounter.
Aftermath: deputies render aid / secure the scene with two people dead and one of their own wounded. Denouement and human cost.
Internal-affairs interview detail that corroborates or complicates the on-scene footage — connective tissue for the documentary, and a potential contradiction source to watch for.
